bug_semantics: An unauthenticated POST to the WebUI /ui/login endpoint resolves the submitted userpass identity before attempting password authentication. A nonexistent username receives an account/identity-not-found response, while an existing username with a wrong password reaches token authentication and receives a different authentication-failure response, exposing username existence through response content.
flaw_origin: Commit b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f first added the public legacy WebUI userpass login route and its log_in function in lib/rucio/web/ui/common/utils.py. The new handler called identity.list_accounts_for_identity, returned 'No accounts for the given identity.' for an empty mapping, and returned 'Cannot get auth token' only after a mapped identity failed password authentication. Later restructuring and the Flask implementation preserved or ported this already-existing response oracle rather than originating it.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f shows the sole parent e75339cee988fc4180fdafb1333aaafe5a08ebfc, human author and committer Ruturaj <ruturaj2305@gmail.com>, and only the message 'WebUI: Resolve Conflicts'; it contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI attribution, or other AI trailer.
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/rucio/rucio/security/advisories/GHSA-38wq-6q2w-hcf9 identifies the unauthenticated /ui/login response oracle, quotes the different nonexistent-user and wrong-password messages, and lists patched versions 35.8.3, 38.5.4, and 39.3.1.

The disputed claims were primary b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f with parent e75339cee988fc4180fdafb1333aaafe5a08ebfc versus reviewer 0f88777af4716552155edfd99731eff2571d4f7b with parent f49c5c9599e147823110dc6da22a0bc33a881f8e. git log --all --reverse -S'No accounts for the given identity.' -- lib/rucio/web/ui/common/utils.py returns b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f as the first writer. git diff e75339cee988fc4180fdafb1333aaafe5a08ebfc b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f shows that commit adding log_in, the identity-existence early response, the later token-failure response, and the userpass authentication dispatch.

git grep at b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f finds def log_in at common/utils.py:158, list_accounts_for_identity(..., 'userpass') at line 190, 'No accounts for the given identity.' at line 192, and 'Cannot get auth token' at line 215. It also finds main.py's /login route and call to log_in plus the login form action /ui/login. The same route/handler grep in e75339cee988fc4180fdafb1333aaafe5a08ebfc returns no matches; its only list_accounts_for_identity matches are unrelated x509 paths. git cat-file -p confirms e75339cee988fc4180fdafb1333aaafe5a08ebfc is the BIC's sole immediate parent, directly resolving introducer_parent and proving parent absence.

The reviewer candidate is a rejected port/import, not the flaw origin. git merge-base --is-ancestor b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f f49c5c9599e147823110dc6da22a0bc33a881f8e succeeds, and git grep in reviewer parent f49c5c9599e147823110dc6da22a0bc33a881f8e:lib/rucio/web/ui/common/utils.py already finds both the explicit no-account responses and the distinct cannot-get-auth-token responses. Thus the absence of the new Flask file in that parent is path absence, not vulnerability absence. The later d8f7c9e943500f0ef0fc705a200d50f436d22605 landing adds an entire Flask tree while its parent still contains the vulnerable legacy implementation, confirming a framework port. By contrast, git diff-tree for b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f shows a cohesive one-parent WebUI login feature with no rename/move status, so there is no squash aggregate to decompose.

Version-boundary checks succeed for git merge-base --is-ancestor b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f against each last-vulnerable tag 35.8.2, 38.5.3, and 39.3.0. git diff of 0b22b350201bcf040aa1aade476cf69944019d97 against its parent shows the direct fix eliminating the missing-account early disclosure and using generic authentication-failed responses for both missing accounts and token failures. Stable git patch-id is 5a814d04e90425e50502170b13aa61d42f9de09b for the direct fix and for backports 33bc01dc055c8e52a688404068419c916fab797f, 949ff8cfd7efb51c71cdceb5e80be8f6858e0b73, and 1ea6771b43c7ae45485486692189e40fbe61f496.

Release ancestry independently confirms each backport is contained in its first-patched tag but absent from the preceding tag: 33bc01dc055c8e52a688404068419c916fab797f is in 35.8.3 and not 35.8.2; 949ff8cfd7efb51c71cdceb5e80be8f6858e0b73 is in 38.5.4 and not 38.5.3; 1ea6771b43c7ae45485486692189e40fbe61f496 is in 39.3.1 and not 39.3.0. git cat-file -p on the resolved BIC provides only human authorship and no AI signal.
reasoning: The primary claim wins both assigned disagreements. The security flaw is the observable decision structure, not the later wording or Flask pathname: existence is tested before password authentication, and the two outcomes produce distinguishable pages. b1f36e5196005dcad2b9b6748531fb61c56f5a9f is the earliest commit that writes that mechanism and exposes it through /ui/login, while its direct parent e75339cee988fc4180fdafb1333aaafe5a08ebfc lacks the handler, route, userpass lookup, and userpass token call. The reviewer's 0f88777af4716552155edfd99731eff2571d4f7b choice only creates a Flask copy when its own parent already has the same vulnerable behavior in the legacy implementation, so treating the missing Flask path as parent absence violates the protocol's rejection of imports and moves. The selected BIC is an ordinary one-parent feature commit rather than a squash landing. The verified direct fix and patch-equivalent backports match every advisory version boundary. Because the resolved BIC commit object contains no AI attribution signal, the gate-complete BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI.
